correctness.rationale: For each edge of type {a,b}, D=2N-a-b-2 and the weighted sum S of neighbour degrees is 4N^2-8N-2Q+4+(4-3N)(a+b)+2(a^2+b^2), with Q the second part-size power sum. The first two colour rounds determine D and S, hence a+b, a^2+b^2 and ab, which uniquely determine the unordered size pair. The within-part and equal-size part-permutation subgroup acts transitively on edges of a given type, proving equality with the full orbit partition. The exact zero/one/two case distinction follows, and the minimal eight-root-vertex collision follows because two unequal unordered positive-integer pairs sharing a sum require at least four parts with total size eight, uniquely {1,3} and {2,2}. Direct finite refinement (114 cases/4,558 aggregate line vertices), independent integer moment comparisons (3,424 tuples/481,572 comparisons), and seven complete graph automorphism enumerations all passed. These checks are corroborative, not substitutes for the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Compared statements and implications of accessible published foundational colour-refinement sources, same-object multipartite line-graph sources, relevant published mathematical statements and related Johnson, rook, and tree line-graph claims. The Arvind et al. refinable-graph framework and Johnson examples do not imply an exact two-round unbalanced multipartite orbit partition. Tananyan treats domination games on this family. Key and Seneviratne study codes on balanced instances; available material provides no second-round invariant, and the full text remained inaccessible. value.rationale: The object is a natural entire infinite graph family, rather than an arbitrary finite slice. The theorem completely determines every stable orbit, its size, and the exact initial refinement depth for arbitrarily large and unbalanced multipartite sizes. The minimal eight-vertex obstruction and an unbounded sharp family identify where first-round degree information provably fails. The substantive invariant is the recoverability of unordered endpoint part sizes from two local moment statistics, which supplies a reusable structural mechanism and a motivated exact boundary for counting refinement; this is not a mere unknown numerical statistic or relabeling.
